rows.responsibility: Durable multi-window restore: bounded versioned serialization, account/user identity fencing, debounced save, exactly-once restore offer, unlock/activation gating, async peer/topic/sublist batch resolution, unavailable/close recovery, reopen-last-closed, navigation-stack replay and placement restore.
rows.state_machine: Saved state is bounded/fail-closed; restore waits for account+unlock, fences each step by session/id, resolves peers/topics/sublist before handoff, preserves close/unavailable as reopenable state, and finishes only when pending steps drain.
rows.side_effects: Canonical navigation/resource/window/account state only through existing owners.
rows.failure_cases: corrupt persistence; account-index reuse to wrong user; stale session callback; unresolved peer/topic; duplicate window; restore while locked; close race; off-screen geometry; replay into unavailable thread
rows.fabushi_target: `source/electron-main/window-state-persistence.ts` and `window-chrome.ts` are partial existing owners; extend them with a source-neutral multi-window restore coordinator plus canonical Account/Conversation routing.
rows.production_evidence: Current `window-state-persistence.ts` atomically persists a single main-window placement and clamps displays, but does not implement account/conversation multi-window restore, identity fencing or reopen-last-closed; gap remains open.
rows.test_evidence: Focused state/persistence/permission/cancellation tests plus descendant exact-head Actions and packaged E2E required.
